extracted.intended_audience: startup founders, PR/communications professionals, and marketing teams crafting executive-hire press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and evaluating a press release announcing a senior/executive hire (C-level or similarly material hire), including when to issue one, structure (headline, lede, body, boilerplate), quote guidance, multimedia requirements, and a short quality checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: C-level hire (when worth doing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue an executive-hire press release for C-level hire (CEO, CTO, CFO, COO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target material, company-defining leadership changes; reserved for top executives whose appointment matters to external stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Famous/recognized executive joining (when worth doing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue when a famous or recognized executive is joining the company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High public recognition increases newsworthiness and distribution value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant board addition (when worth doing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue when a significant board addition occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board appointments that materially change governance or credibility warrant announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hire signals strategic shift (when worth doing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue when the hire signals a strategic shift for the company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the announcement to contextualize how the hire enables new direction or priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hire validates market positioning (when worth doing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue when the hire validates the company's market positioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hiring that confirms market strategy or product-market fit is newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Junior or mid-level hires (when NOT worth doing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not issue press releases for junior or mid-level hires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve public releases for materially newsworthy roles; avoid cluttering outreach with low-impact hires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lateral moves without significance (when NOT worth doing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid releases for lateral moves that lack strategic significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the move doesn't change role scope or signal strategy, skip a press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal promotions for non-named roles (when NOT worth doing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't announce internal promotions that aren't named or notable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named, high-impact promotions may be fine; anonymous/internal-only movements should not be publicized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanity titles (when NOT worth doing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid press releases for hires that are primarily 'vanity titles.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles without substantive new authority or responsibility are not newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-day announcements (when NOT worth doing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't issue releases for single-day announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ephemeral or event-specific hires that lack ongoing relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline format
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested headline templates: "[Executive Name] Joins [Company] as [Title]" or "[Company] Hires [Executive Name] to Lead [Specific Function/Strategy]".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, declarative headlines that include name and role or the strategic function the hire will lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede (opening sentence template)
rubrics_metrics.description: "[Company] today announced that [Executive Name] has joined as [Title], where [he/she/they] will [specific responsibility]. [Name] joins from [previous company], where [he/she/they] [specific accomplishment]."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-load the who/what/why: role, primary responsibility, and relevant prior accomplishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body Para 1 — Why This Hire
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain company stage and context, what this role enables, and the strategic priorities this addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear why the hire matters now — link the role to concrete company needs and strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body Para 2 — Executive Background
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide 3-5 most relevant prior roles, specific accomplishments, education, and industry recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the most relevant credentials and measurable accomplishments that justify the hire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body Para 3 — What They'll Do
rubrics_metrics.description: State specific priorities for the first 90 days, long-term strategic objectives, and reporting relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concrete about immediate focus areas and where the executive sits in the org chart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body Para 4 — Quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a CEO quote on why this hire and a new-executive quote on why this opportunity; quotes should be substantive, not generic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide distinct viewpoints: CEO explains rationale; exec explains motivation and vision. Avoid platitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard company description; mention any leadership team context; stage and scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep boilerplate concise and consistent across company announcements; include relevant metrics or descriptors.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEO quote guidance (bad vs good)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bad example: "We are thrilled to welcome [Name] to the team. Their experience will be invaluable as we scale." Good example: "For the past year, we've been searching for a leader who could take our [specific area] from [current state] to [future state]. [Name]'s track record at [Company] doing exactly this is why I'm confident we have the right person."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer quotes that explain the strategic need and cite the new hire's track record in relevant terms; avoid generic praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive quote guidance (bad vs good)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bad example: "I'm excited to join such a dynamic team." Good example: "Three things drew me here: [specific reason 1], [specific reason 2], and [specific reason 3]. I'm joining at a moment when [specific market/product condition] makes this work uniquely consequential."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exec quotes should enumerate concrete reasons for joining and situate the opportunity in market/product context rather than expressing generic enthusiasm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia requirement — professional headshot
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a professional headshot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality, press-ready image is expected; listed as required in Multimedia Requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia option — video of new executive
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional: video of new executive on company vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use video to add personality and deeper explanation, but it's optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia option — photo with CEO
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional: photo with CEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for visual storytelling about leadership handoff or partnership; optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — hire is genuinely material
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the hire is genuinely material to company narrative or operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the hire is not material, do not issue a press release; materiality is a primary gate for newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — background substantively detailed
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the executive background is substantively detailed in the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release should include measurable, relevant accomplishments and 3–5 prior roles rather than vague CV bullet points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — specific responsibilities outlined
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that specific responsibilities are outlined (first 90 days, long-term objectives, reporting relationship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague role descriptions; provide concrete priorities and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — substantive quotes from both sides
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm the presence of substantive quotes from CEO and new executive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes should explain rationale and motivations with specifics, not generic praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — professional headshot included
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm a professional headshot is included with the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Image availability affects pickup by media; include one by default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality rubric — strategic rationale clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the strategic rationale for the hire is clearly stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release should make it obvious how the hire advances company strategy or addresses specific needs.
